license_required.quote: It shall be unlawful for any person to engage in the practice of osteopathic medicine and surgery, or pretend to a knowledge of any branch or branches of osteopathic medicine and surgery, or to hold himself out as a practitioner in osteopathic medicine and surgery, or to assume the title of Doctor of Osteopathic Medicine and Surgery or doctor of any specific disease, or to diagnose diseases or to treat diseases by the use of osteopathic medicine and surgery or by any other means, or to sign any birth or death certificate unless otherwise authorized by law, or to hold himself out as able to do so, unless he has received a certificate of licensure or permission from the board

issuing_authority.quote: The State Board of Osteopathic Medicine in the Department of State.

name.quote: The State Board of Osteopathic Medicine in the Department of State.

type.quote: The State Board of Osteopathic Medicine shall consist of the Commissioner of Professional and Occupational Affairs or a designee; the Secretary of Health or a designee; two members appointed by the Governor who shall be persons representing the public at large

umbrella_agency.quote: The State Board of Osteopathic Medicine in the Department of State.

moral_character_required.quote: A graduate of an osteopathic medical college in the United States who seeks licensure by the board shall furnish the board with evidence, prior to any examination, that he is of good moral character

degree_required.quote: A graduate of an osteopathic medical college in the United States who seeks licensure by the board shall furnish the board with evidence, prior to any examination, that he is of good moral character, is not addicted to habit-forming drugs, and has completed the educational requirements prescribed by the board.

accrediting_body.quote: An osteopathic medical college. degree_level.quote: A graduate of an osteopathic medical college qualifying under this act may, on receiving his degree as a doctor of osteopathy, apply to the board for a temporary graduate license

exams.name: National Board or Flex examination
exams.notes: Board may also accept other state or territorial examinations acceptable to the board. Endorsement pathway available for currently licensed physicians who qualify by National Board or Flex.
exams.quote: Whenever an applicant fails an examination he shall have, after the expiration of six months and within two years, the privilege of a second examination by the board. If he fails the second examination he shall apply de novo after a year of graduate study approved by the board

interval_years.quote: Such renewal period shall not be longer than two years.

required.quote: The board shall adopt, promulgate and enforce rules and regulations establishing requirements for continuing medical education to be met by persons licensed to practice osteopathic medicine without restriction.

period_years.quote: Each person licensed to practice osteopathic medicine and surgery without restriction, during the two-year period immediately preceding a biennial date for reregistering with the board, must complete a program of continuing medical education, as defined by and acceptable to the board.

available.quote: The board may accept by endorsement currently licensed osteopathic physicians qualified by either the National Board or by Flex examination or by any other state or territorial examination acceptable to the board for the purpose of licensure.

requirements.value: Board may accept by endorsement currently licensed osteopathic physicians qualified by National Board, Flex examination, or any other state or territorial examination acceptable to the board. Border-state physicians may also practice in PA if they file a certified copy of their license and the adjoining state reciprocates.
requirements.quote: The board may accept by endorsement currently licensed osteopathic physicians qualified by either the National Board or by Flex examination or by any other state or territorial examination acceptable to the board for the purpose of licensure.

exists.quote: The State Board of Osteopathic Medicine shall consist of the Commissioner of Professional and Occupational Affairs or a designee; the Secretary of Health or a designee; two members appointed by the Governor who shall be persons representing the public at large; one member appointed by the Governor who is a physician assistant; one member appointed by the Governor who shall be a respiratory therapist, a perfusionist or a licensed athletic trainer; and seven members appointed by the Governor who shall be graduates of a legally incorporated and reputable college of osteopathic medicine

national_association.quote: the educational qualifications for acceptance as a matriculant in an osteopathic medical college incorporated within the Commonwealth and the curricula and training to be offered by such colleges shall meet the requirements set by the board after advice and consultation with the appropriate committees of the American Osteopathic Association or any other accrediting body which is recognized by the board.

regulatory_model.quote: It shall be unlawful for any person to practice or attempt to offer to practice osteopathic medicine, as defined in this act, without having at the time of so doing a valid, unexpired, unrevoked and unsuspended license issued under this act.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Failing to demonstrate the qualifications or standards for a license provided in this act or board regulations.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Failing to demonstrate the qualifications or standards for a license provided in this act or the regulations of the board.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Making misleading, deceptive, untrue or fraudulent representations in practice or in obtaining a license.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Making misleading, deceptive, untrue or fraudulent representations in the practice of osteopathic medicine and surgery, practicing fraud or deceit in obtaining a license to practice osteopathic medicine and surgery, or making a false or deceptive biennial registration with the board.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Conviction of a felony, a crime involving moral turpitude, or a crime related to the practice of osteopathic medicine.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Conviction of a felony, a crime involving moral turpitude, or a crime related to the practice of osteopathic medicine.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Having a license to practice osteopathic medicine revoked or suspended, or other disciplinary action taken, in another jurisdiction.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Having a license to practice osteopathic medicine and surgery revoked or suspended or having other disciplinary action taken, or an application for a license refused, revoked or suspended by the proper licensing authority of another state, territory or country.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Being unable to practice with reasonable skill and safety due to illness, drunkenness, drug use, or mental or physical condition.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Being unable to practice osteopathic medicine and surgery with reasonable skill and safety to patients by reason of illness, drunkenness, excessive use of drugs, narcotics, chemicals, or other type of material, or as a result of any mental or physical condition.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Violating a regulation promulgated by the board or a prior board disciplinary order.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Violating a regulation promulgated by the board or an order of the board previously entered by it in a disciplinary proceeding.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Knowingly maintaining a professional connection with someone violating the act, or aiding an unlicensed person to practice osteopathic medicine.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Knowingly maintaining a professional connection or association with a person who is in violation of this act or the regulations of the board or knowingly aiding, assisting, procuring or advising an unlicensed person to practice osteopathic medicine and surgery contrary to this act, or the regulations of the board.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Being guilty of immoral or unprofessional conduct, including departure from acceptable and prevailing osteopathic medical practice.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Being guilty of immoral or unprofessional conduct. Unprofessional conduct shall include any departure from, or the failure to conform to, the standards of acceptable and prevailing osteopathic medical practice. Actual injury to a patient need not be established.

definition_quote.value: The art and science having for its object the cure of disease and the preservation of the health of man with or without drugs, except healing by spiritual means or prayer.
definition_quote.quote: The art and science having for its object the cure of disease and the preservation of the health of man with or without drugs, except healing by spiritual means or prayer.

methods_authorized.quote: Osteopathic medicine and surgery. The art and science having for its object the cure of disease and the preservation of the health of man with or without drugs, except healing by spiritual means or prayer.

drug_authority.value: Osteopathic physicians may prescribe drugs as part of the practice of osteopathic medicine and surgery; clinical clerks may not prescribe drugs.
drug_authority.quote: Nothing contained in this act shall be construed to entitle a clinical clerk to practice medicine or surgery or to prescribe drugs.

license_types_available.quote: The board may grant the following licenses: (1) Unrestricted license. (2) Temporary graduate license. (3) Short-term camp physician license.

temporary_graduate_license_duration_mont.quote: A temporary graduate license shall be valid for 12 months thereafter and shall be recognized only as conferring upon the licensee the right to participate in approved graduate osteopathic or medical training within the complex of the hospital to which he is assigned.

short_term_license_available.quote: A short-term license valid for a period not to exceed three months may be granted by the board to osteopathic physicians licensed and in good standing in other states or Canada who intend to practice osteopathic medicine as osteopathic physicians in camps in the Commonwealth.

visiting_team_physician_exemption.quote: A physician who is licensed in good standing to practice in another state or country shall be exempt from the licensure requirements of this act while practicing in this Commonwealth if either of the following apply

drug_addiction_bar.quote: A graduate of an osteopathic medical college in the United States who seeks licensure by the board shall furnish the board with evidence, prior to any examination, that he is of good moral character, is not addicted to habit-forming drugs

felony_drug_conviction_waiting_period_ye.quote: An applicant who has been convicted of a felonious act prohibited by the act of April 14, 1972 (P.L.233, No.64), known as 'The Controlled Substance, Drug, Device and Cosmetic Act,' or convicted of a felony relating to a controlled substance in a court of law of the United States or any other state, territory or country shall not be licensed unless: (1) at least ten years have elapsed from the date of conviction

multi_state_license_reporting_required.quote: Any licensed osteopathic physician of this Commonwealth who is also licensed to practice osteopathic medicine or surgery in any other state, territory or country or any other board-regulated practitioner licensed or certified to practice in any other state, territory or country shall report this information to the board on the biennial registration application. Any disciplinary action taken in other states shall be reported to the board on the biennial registration application or within 90 days of final disposition, whichever is sooner.

impaired_professional_program_available.quote: The board may defer and ultimately dismiss any of the types of corrective action set forth in this act for an impaired professional so long as the professional is progressing satisfactorily in an approved treatment program

mandatory_impairment_reporting_required.quote: Any hospital or health care facility, peer or colleague who has substantial evidence that a professional has an active addictive disease for which the professional is not receiving treatment, is diverting a controlled substance or is mentally or physically incompetent to carry out the duties of his or her license shall make or cause to be made a report to the board

license_revocation_reinstatement_waiting.quote: Any person whose license, certificate or registration has been revoked may apply for reinstatement after a period of at least five years

value: Commitment to an institution due to mental incompetency
Conviction of a felony under The Controlled Substance, Drug, Device and Cosmetic Act
Conviction of an offense under laws of another jurisdiction which would be a felony under The Controlled Substance, Drug, Device and Cosmetic Act if committed in Pennsylvania
automatic_suspension_triggers.quote: A license or certificate issued under this act shall automatically be suspended upon the commitment to an institution of a licensee because of mental incompetency from any cause upon filing with the board a certified copy of such commitment, conviction of a felony under the act of April 14, 1972 (P.L.233, No.64), known as 'The Controlled Substance, Drug, Device and Cosmetic Act,' or conviction of an offense under the laws of another jurisdiction, which, if committed in Pennsylvania, would be a felony under 'The Controlled Substance, Drug, Device and Cosmetic Act.'

physician_assistant_supervision_ratio_ma.quote: There shall be no more than six physician assistants for whom a physician has responsibility or supervises pursuant to a written agreement at any time.

physician_assistant_written_agreement_re.quote: The primary supervising physician shall file, or cause to be filed, with the board a written agreement that identifies the manner in which the physician assistant will assist the primary supervising physician

physician_assistant_countersignature_req.value: The primary supervising physician determines countersignature requirements in the written agreement, except that the approved physician must countersign 100% of patient records within 10 days during the first 12 months post-graduation and the first 12 months in a new specialty.
physician_assistant_countersignature_req.quote: The primary supervising physician shall determine countersignature requirements of patient records completed by the physician assistant in a written agreement, except as provided for in paragraph (4). (4) The approved physician shall countersign 100% of the patient records completed by the physician assistant within a reasonable time, which shall not exceed 10 days

physician_assistant_prescribing_authorit.value: A physician assistant may prescribe and dispense drugs only at the direction of a licensed physician; the board and State Board of Pharmacy will jointly develop regulations. A physician assistant may not independently prescribe or dispense drugs.
physician_assistant_prescribing_authorit.quote: Nothing in this act shall be construed to permit a physician assistant to independently prescribe or dispense drugs. The board and State Board of Pharmacy will jointly develop regulations to permit a physician assistant to prescribe and dispense drugs at the direction of a licensed physician.

physician_assistant_liability_insurance_.quote: A licensed physician assistant in this Commonwealth shall maintain a level of professional liability insurance coverage in the minimum amount of $1,000,000 per occurrence or claims made.

perfusionist_liability_insurance_minimum.quote: A licensed perfusionist practicing in this Commonwealth shall maintain a level of professional liability insurance coverage in the minimum amount of $1,000,000 per occurrence or claims made.

genetic_counselor_liability_insurance_mi.quote: A licensee under this section, practicing in this Commonwealth, shall maintain a level of professional liability insurance coverage in the minimum amount of $1,000,000 per occurrence or claims made.

radiologic_procedures_auxiliary_personne.value: On and after January 1, 1988, auxiliary personnel may perform radiologic procedures on an osteopathic physician's premises only under direct supervision of an osteopathic physician and only if the person has passed a board-approved examination; for therapeutic radiologic procedures, the osteopathic physician must be on the premises.
radiologic_procedures_auxiliary_personne.quote: On and after January 1, 1988, no auxiliary personnel shall perform radiologic procedures on the premises of an osteopathic physician unless such person is under the direct supervision of an osteopathic physician and unless such person has passed an examination approved by the board and administered in accordance with section 812.1 of the act of April 9, 1929, provided that no such auxiliary personnel shall perform radiologic procedures for therapeutic purposes unless the osteopathic physician under whose direct supervision such auxiliary personnel is acting is on the premises at the time the radiologic procedures are performed.

athletic_trainer_direction_model.value: Athletic trainers practice under the direction of a licensed physician, dentist or podiatrist via referral or written protocol; physical presence of the supervising physician is not required if the supervising physician is readily available for consultation by direct communication, radio, telephone, facsimile, telecommunications or via other electronic means.
athletic_trainer_direction_model.quote: Supervision over the actions of a licensed athletic trainer via referral by prescription to treat conditions for a physically active person from a licensed physician, dentist or podiatrist or written protocol approved by a supervising physician, dentist or podiatrist, except that the physical presence of the supervising physician, dentist or podiatrist is not required if the supervising physician, dentist or podiatrist is readily available for consultation by direct communication, radio, telephone, facsimile, telecommunications or via other electronic means.

board_regulated_allied_professions.quote: An osteopathic physician, physician assistant, respiratory therapist or licensed athletic trainer or an applicant for a license or certificate issued by the board.

osteopathic_college_accrediting_body.quote: An institution of higher learning accredited by the American Osteopathic Association, its successors and assigns, as an agency to provide courses in the arts and sciences of medicine and related subjects and empowered to grant academic degrees in osteopathic medicine and surgery.

approved_hospital_required_for_graduate_.quote: Approved hospital. A hospital which has been approved by the board for providing supervised graduate osteopathic medical training.

continuing_education_excluded_topics.quote: No credit shall be given for any course in office management or practice building.
